hints: Focus on working out how many fluorines must be bonded to use up all the outer electrons with no lone pair left.
Arsenic is in Group 15 so it must form 5 bonds to give $\text{AsF}_5$, while selenium in Group 16 must form 6 bonds to give $\text{SeF}_6$.
Compare trigonal bipyramidal with octahedral and remember to ignore $180^\circ$, then count how many different remaining angles each shape has.
walkthrough:
**Find the formulae from no lone pair**

Arsenic is Group 15 with 5 outer electrons. To have zero lone pairs with normal covalent bonds, all 5 electrons must be used in 5 bonds. So the compound is $\text{AsF}_5$.

Selenium is Group 16 with 6 outer electrons. To have zero lone pairs, all 6 electrons must be used in 6 bonds. So the compound is $\text{SeF}_6$.

**Predict the shapes**

For $\text{AsF}_5$, there are 5 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs. This is trigonal bipyramidal.

For $\text{SeF}_6$, there are 6 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs. This is octahedral.

**Count the bond angles ignoring 180 degrees**

Trigonal bipyramidal has angles of $90^\circ$, $120^\circ$ and $180^\circ$. Ignoring $180^\circ$, two different angles remain: $90^\circ$ and $120^\circ$.

$$\text{trigonal bipyramidal: } 90^\circ \text{ and } 120^\circ \text{ (plus } 180^\circ \text{ ignored)}$$

**Check selenium fluoride**

Octahedral has angles of $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ only. Ignoring $180^\circ$, only one angle remains: $90^\circ$.

$$\text{octahedral: } 90^\circ \text{ only (plus } 180^\circ \text{ ignored)}$$ 
So only arsenic fluoride has two different bond angles.

options.A: Incorrect. Arsenic fluoride ($\text{AsF}_5$, trigonal bipyramidal) does have $90^\circ$ and $120^\circ$, but selenium fluoride ($\text{SeF}_6$, octahedral) has only $90^\circ$ once $180^\circ$ is ignored.
options.B: Correct. $\text{AsF}_5$ is trigonal bipyramidal with $90^\circ$ and $120^\circ$ (ignoring $180^\circ$), so two angles. $\text{SeF}_6$ is octahedral with only $90^\circ$ (ignoring $180^\circ$), so one angle.
options.C: Incorrect. It reverses the logic. Selenium fluoride is highly symmetrical octahedral, so all adjacent F-Se-F angles are $90^\circ$. It is arsenic fluoride that has the extra $120^\circ$ angle.
options.D: Incorrect. Arsenic fluoride definitely has two angles. Students choosing this often think trigonal bipyramidal has only one angle or forget that axial to equatorial ($90^\circ$) differs from equatorial to equatorial ($120^\circ$).
